cases.expected: Non‑null instance of URIFactory that equals the factory created by the default builder
cases.description: When a JsonSchemaFactory is created via the default `JsonSchemaFactory.builder().build()` the internal `uriFactory` is instantiated with the library's default implementation. The test verifies that `getUriFactory()` returns a non‑null object and that the returned reference is the same object that the builder used to construct the factory.

cases.expected: Non‑null instance of the custom URIFactory supplied to the builder, and it is the exact same object (reference equality).
cases.description: Create a custom implementation of `URIFactory` (e.g., a stub that always returns a fixed URI). Build a `JsonSchemaFactory` with `JsonSchemaFactory.builder().uriFactory(customFactory).build()`. Verify that `getUriFactory()` returns a non‑null object and that `factory.getUriFactory() == customFactory`.

cases.expected: The returned URIFactory is the same instance that was present in the blueprint factory.
cases.description: Create a blueprint factory using a custom `URIFactory` as in the previous case. Then build a new factory with `JsonSchemaFactory.builder(blueprint).build()`. Assert that the new factory’s `getUriFactory()` reference equals the blueprint’s `getUriFactory()` reference.

cases.expected: The returned URIFactory is the default implementation when the blueprint is created with the default builder.
cases.description: Create a blueprint factory using the default builder (`JsonSchemaFactory.builder().build()`). Build a second factory from this blueprint (`JsonSchemaFactory.builder(blueprint).build()`). Verify that both factories expose the same default `URIFactory` instance.

cases.expected: Identical object reference on successive calls.
cases.description: For any `JsonSchemaFactory` instance (default, custom, or blueprint‑derived), invoke `getUriFactory()` multiple times and assert that each call returns the exact same object (`factory.getUriFactory() == factory.getUriFactory()`). This ensures the method does not create a new instance on each invocation.

Attempt to create a factory with `JsonSchemaFactory.builder(null)`. The expected behavior is that the method validates its argument and throws a `NullPointerException`. This test confirms that the factory does not silently fallback to a default URI factory when a null blueprint is supplied.
